• N tag means the current word is not a pun.
• P tag means the current word is a pun.

• B tag indicates that the current word appears before the pun in the given context.
• P tag highlights the current word is a pun.
• A tag indicates that the current word appears after the pun.

This new tagging scheme, BPA, is used throughout the rest of the paper and is shown to be effective in handling both homographic and heterographic puns.

In AddOneSent, each passage contains a human-approved random sentence that may be unrelated to the passage. This is done to test how well the model performs when faced with completely unrelated information.

By using these datasets, the authors can examine whether a model is robust to noise or not by seeing how well it performs in the presence of misleading sentences.

Gaussian-masked directional multi-head attention is described as a function to map queries and key-value pairs to the representation of input. It is similar to scaled dot-product attention in the original Transformer, but with two key differences: it uses a Gaussian-masked directional attention mechanism instead of standard self-attention, and it captures information from different dimension positions.

In this equation, AG represents the application of Gaussian-masked directional attention. This mechanism expects to pay attention to the adjacent characters of each position and cast the localness relationship between characters as a fix Gaussian weight for attention.
